newsitem.title: UK: London dealers cautiously optimistic for gold.
newsitem.headline: London dealers cautiously optimistic for gold.

text.p: Precious metals dealers voiced cautious optimism that gold prices could push higher on Thursday although they admitted that a rally would attract heavy selling.
"I'm cautiously optimistic although at the moment gold seems to be stuck in a $382.50-$384.00 range," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $383.00 per ounce after $382.65 in the morning and a close on Wednesday of $383.80/$384.30.
"There has been a bit of producer selling around at the top end of the range but there has also been customer and physical business," a dealer said.
"The professionals keep selling it and having to pay to get it back," the dealer added.

Most of the impetus for this week's firmer tone was coming from the hugely cash rich and mainly U.S-run hedge funds which had decided that the gold price was not going to fall from the $377-$379 level it had occupied since the end of October.
The funds covering short positions sparked fresh buying and lifted prices from around $378 at the end of last week.
"I think the potential is there (for gold) but it all depends on the funds," one dealer in continental Europe said.
Also helping gold and platinum and palladium as well, was a weaker dollar against the yen which had shaded the booming U.S. equity and bond markets and made platinum cheaper in Japan.
Dealers said they thought around $382.00 would be about the bottom of the current price cycle.

"The market looks a bit freer than for a few weeks and we might see a bit more volatility between now and the end of the year," one dealer said, explaining that the cash price seemed less strangled by defensive plays from options writers.
Dealers noted heavy buying of February and December call options at the $390 strike price and Februaries at $400.
Cash silver was indicated at $4.92/$4.94 up a cent as Comex players attempted to challenge the $4.95 resistance on the December contract.
"If it gets through that, it could get up to $5.01, $5.05 on the exchange," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium held gains aided by the dollar continuing weaker against the yen. Platinum was indicated at $386.50/$387.50 down 30 cents.
Palladium matched its morning six-week high fix this afternoon and was indicated at $120.50/$121.50, down $0.25.
